steps.say: Not every brain tumour grows from brain tissue. The commonest benign one grows from the coverings, and that changes the whole operation.
steps.tx: **Meningiomas** (dura cover tumours) are dural-based **extra-axial masses** (outside brain lumps) with a **dural tail** (dura streak), homogeneous enhancement, **hyperostosis** (thickened bone) of adjacent skull and a CSF cleft, separating them confidently from intra-axial gliomas on contrast MRI, and slow growth lets incidental lumps under 2 cm watch safely.

vis.alt: Contrast MRI panels showing enhancing dural-based meningioma mass.
vis.caption: Dural-based enhancing meningioma on contrast MRI. Credit: Hellerhoff via Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: Grade beats size for decisions. Brain invasion alone makes a tumour atypical, whatever the microscope counts.
steps.tx: WHO grades run **1 benign** (slow grade), **2 atypical** (middle grade) with **4 to 19 mitoses** (dividing cells) or **brain invasion** (finger into brain), and **3 anaplastic** (wild grade) with **20 or more mitoses** (many dividing cells) per 10 high-power fields, and grade drives adjuvant decisions more than size, while TERT or CDKN2A loss makes grade 3 and chordoid or clear-cell pattern makes grade 2.

vis.alt: Meningioma histology with whorls, psammoma bodies and uniform nuclei.
vis.caption: Meningioma whorls and psammoma bodies on histology. Credit: Mikael Haggstrom via Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: Simpson grades the surgeon's work, not the tumour. Grade one of a surface lump cures, while skull base work deliberately stops short.
steps.tx: **Simpson grades** (removal completeness scale) record resection from **I** (grade 1, tumour, dura and bone removed) to **V** (grade 5, biopsy only), and Simpson I of a **convexity meningioma** (surface lump) is effectively **curative resection** (healing removal) with low recurrence near 10 percent, quoted at each grade to guide follow-up intensity.

steps.say: Deep skull base lumps trade completeness for nerves. Planned leftovers get radiosurgery instead of risky chasing.
steps.tx: **Skull base meningiomas** (deep base lumps) of the olfactory groove, sphenoid wing and petroclival region accept planned **subtotal resection** (partial removal) with **radiosurgery** (focused ray treatment) to the cavernous or petrous remnant to preserve cranial nerves and carotid flow, and cavernous sinus work avoids carotid injury above all.

steps.say: Radiation follows grade and leftovers, not every patient. Fully removed benign lumps need only scans.
steps.tx: **Adjuvant radiotherapy** (extra ray treatment) follows subtotal (**grade 2 STR**) or recurrent **grade 2 disease** (middle grade leftover) and all **grade 3 tumours** (wild grade) per EANO 2021 principles, with ROAM and EORTC 22042 testing rays after gross total grade 2 removal, while fully resected grade 1 needs only surveillance MRI at lengthening intervals.

steps.say: Spine lumps favour middle-aged women and the mid back. Removing them with their dural patch usually ends the myelopathy.
steps.tx: **Spinal meningiomas** (cord cover lumps) favour the thoracic dura in middle-aged women with **psammoma bodies** (round calcium pearls), and Simpson I resection through a posterior approach with dural excision usually cures back pain and **myelopathy** (cord pressure illness), with bladder symptoms prompting urgent decompression.

steps.say: Many lumps plus deafness means a gene, not chance. Families need scanning from head to tail.
steps.tx: Multiple meningiomas with bilateral **vestibular schwannomas** (hearing nerve lumps) mark **NF2** (tumour gene illness) with **merlin loss** (missing brake protein), and family members need craniospinal screening with audiometry and MRI, plus genetic counselling covering transmission and yearly checks for at-risk children.

steps.say: Vision loss with a swollen disc and rail tracks around the nerve means sheath tumour. Cutting it blinds, so rays treat it.
steps.tx: **Optic nerve sheath meningiomas** (eye nerve cover lumps) present with painless visual loss and optic disc swelling with a **tram-track sign** (rail lines), and they are irradiated rather than resected because surgery blinds while **radiotherapy** (ray treatment) preserves sight, with vision charted at every visit during treatment.
